basis: Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy; persistent distal muscle atrophy occurs in 4/7 (~57%). Hearing impairment has no established frequency.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: denervation causes established muscle tissue loss in 4/7 (~57%); this is structural atrophy rather than weakness alone.

basis: Motor and speech delay define the neurological phenotype. Precocious puberty occurs in 30-79%; small extremities and hypermobility do not establish skeletal damage.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: precocious puberty represents intrinsic endocrine dysfunction in 30-79%; the supplied concept is defined by developmental delay.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: hypermobility and small extremities occur in 80-99%, but neither establishes destructive skeletal disease or functional joint impairment.

basis: Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; complete AV block and limb contracture each occur in 1/1 assessed patient. Very small denominators limit frequency certainty.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: third-degree AV block is substantive cardiac conduction failure, reported in 1/1 assessed patient; unlike bradycardia alone, it supports cardiac dysfunction.

basis: Metabolic bone disease with disordered remodeling, fractures and osteoarthritis. Renal and cardiovascular findings are occasional (5-29%).

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: Paget disease is a metabolic bone disorder, explicitly supported by its ancestry; the metabolic mechanism axis accompanies the skeletal location.

basis: Developmental, digital and cleft-lip malformations define affected cases; nail hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%. HPO frequencies conflict with the usually asymptomatic exposure description.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cleft lip is an oral structural malformation explicitly included in the embryopathy definition and annotated in 30-79% of affected cases.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: congenital nail aplasia/hypoplasia is structural appendage damage, annotated in 30-79%; it is less central than the defining developmental malformations.

basis: Median nerve compression defines CTS2; established thenar muscle atrophy occurs in 13/14 (~93%), demonstrating persistent muscle tissue loss.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: thenar atrophy in 13/14 (~93%) is lasting denervation-related muscle tissue loss within the syndrome, rather than pain or weakness alone.

basis: Reticuloendothelial disorder with anemia and splenic involvement. Hepatomegaly and jaundice alone do not establish direct hepatic injury; frequencies are unspecified.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatosplenomegaly and jaundice lack evidence of functional hepatic injury or damaging infiltration; jaundice does not distinguish hepatic disease from hemolysis.

basis: Inherited immunodeficiency caused by B-cell maturation failure; circulating B cells are depleted in 44/44. Infections and secondary bronchiectasis are separate diseases.

decisions.haematologic: primary: the defining maturation defect affects blood cells, with near-absent B cells in 44/44; the blood-cell mechanism rule applies alongside immunodeficiency.

basis: Genetically defined autoinflammatory interferonopathy; damaging AGS-like encephalopathy is the predominant presentation (>30% estimated). Skin frequency is uncertain.

decisions.neurologic: involved: AGS-like encephalopathy predominates (>30% estimated), but this umbrella is defined by interferon dysregulation and permits other phenotypes.

basis: Defining renal and pulmonary hamartomatous cysts, renal dysplasia and lung fibrosis. Hypertension is frequent (80-99%) but is a separately diagnosed renal consequence.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension in 80-99% is a separately diagnosed consequence of renal disease; no direct cardiac or vascular lesion is established.
